newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Fernandez sees Argentine labor law before October.
newsitem.headline: Fernandez sees Argentine labor law before October.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said he expects the government, big business and labor to reach an agreement on labor reforms that can become law before mid-term elections in October.

The government, the Group of Eight business chambers and the CGT main labor federation were scheduled to meet late Monday to define where they agree and disagree on proposed reforms to be sent to Congress.

"I think it will be law before October and that the positions of the CGT and the G8 are not that different," Fernandez told Reuters in an interview. "When we go to the small print of the agreement, to the details, the positions will narrow."
The Peronist government desperately needs good news on the 17.3 percent unemployment rate ahead of October's mid-term elections in Congress.

The International Monetary Fund recommended labor reforms as a way of reducing employment costs and President Carlos Menem tried to push a tough reform package through by decree. Blocked by courts and hostile unions, he tried three-way talks, and when they proved fruitless, he made a deal with unions.
Late last month Menem went behind the backs of business leaders to sign a blueprint Act of Agreement with the unions, which was a watered-down reform package.

The big business lobby has blasted it as "useless" as it maintains union control over wage talks and drops plans to replace costly redundancy payouts with unemployment insurance. It also drops plans to force union-controlled health care plans to compete with private firms in an open market.

"The reform is not the most we professional economists want, which is total deregulation of the labor market...but it is preferable to have a reform by consensus that does not have to be argued in the courts," Fernandez said in the interview. (( -- Gary Regenstreif, Buenos Aires Newsroom 541 318-0618))
